column4: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s chosen ones, and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,
column5: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s elect, and the acknowledging of the truth which is after godliness;

column4: in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began;
column5: In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;

column4: but in his own time revealed his word in the message with which I was entrusted according to the commandment of God our Savior;
column5: But hath in due times manifested his word through preaching, which is committed unto me according to the commandment of God our Saviour;

column4: to Titus, my true child according to a common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
column5: To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.

column4: I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you,
column5: For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:

column4: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children who believe, who are not accused of loose or unruly behavior.
column5: If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly.

column4: For the overseer must be blameless, as God’s steward, not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain;
column5: For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre;

column4: but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair, holy, self-controlled,
column5: But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;

column4: holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict those who contradict him.
column5: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.

column4: For there are also many unruly men, vain talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
column5: For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision:

column4: whose mouths must be stopped: men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for dishonest gain’s sake.
column5: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre’s sake.

column4: One of them, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons.”
column5: One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies.

column4: This testimony is true. For this cause, reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
column5: This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;

column4: not paying attention to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.
column5: Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.

column4: To the pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
column5: Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.

column4: They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
column5: They profess that they know God; but in works they deny him , being abominable, and disobedient, and unto every good work reprobate.

column4: But say the things which fit sound doctrine,
column5: But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine:

column4: that older men should be temperate, sensible, sober minded, sound in faith, in love, and in perseverance:
column5: That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.

column4: and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good,
column5: The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;

column4: that they may train the young wives to love their husbands, to love their children,
column5: That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children,

column4: to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.
column5: To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.

column4: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded.
column5: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded.

column4: In all things be showing yourself an example of good works. In your teaching, be showing integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,
column5: In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,

column4: and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.
column5: Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.

column4: Exhort servants to be in subjection to their own masters and to be well-pleasing in all things, not contradicting,
column5: Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things ; not answering again;

column4: not stealing, but showing all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God, our Savior, in all things.
column5: Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.

column4: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
column5: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,

column4: instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;
column5: Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;

column4: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
column5: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;

column4: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
column5: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.

column4: Say these things and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.
column5: These things speak, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no man despise thee.

column4: Remind them to be in subjection to rulers and to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
column5: Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work,

column4: to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
column5: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.

column4: For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
column5: For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

column4: But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
column5: But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,

column4: not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
column5: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;

column4: whom he poured out on us richly, through Jesus Christ our Savior;
column5: Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour;

column4: that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
column5: That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

column4: This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you affirm confidently, so that those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;
column5: This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.

column4: but shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife, and disputes about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.
column5: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

column4: Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning,
column5: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;

column4: knowing that such a one is perverted and sins, being self-condemned.
column5: Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself.

column4: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.
column5: When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.

column4: Send Zenas, the lawyer, and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them.
column5: Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them.

column4: Let our people also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they may not be unfruitful.
column5: And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.

column4: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
column5: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
